# Psalm 60 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the music director. A psalm of David, to be sung to the tune of 'Lily of the Testimony.' A Miktam. David wrote this when he was at war with Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and killed 12,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt.

**2** You have rejected us, O God, and broken our defenses. You have been angry with us; now restore us to Your favor.

**3** You have shaken our land and split it open. Seal the cracks, for the land trembles.

**4** You have been very hard on us, making us drink wine that sent us reeling.

**5** But You have raised a banner for those who fear You — a rallying point in the face of attack. Pause and reflect.

**6** Now rescue Your beloved people. Answer us and save us by Your power.

**7** God has promised this from His sanctuary: 'In triumph I will parcel out Shechem and measure off the valley of Succoth.

**8** Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh, too. Ephraim, My helmet, will produce My warriors, and Judah, My scepter, will produce My kings.

**9** But Moab, My washbasin, will become My servant, and I will wipe My feet on Edom and shout in triumph over Philistia.'

**10** But who will bring me into the fortified city? Who will bring me victory over Edom?

**11** Have You rejected us, O God? Will You no longer march with our armies?

**12** Oh, please help us against our enemies, for all human help is useless.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **60:7-9**: God's oracle divides the world into two categories: Israel's territories (Shechem, Succoth, Gilead, Manasseh, Ephraim, Judah) are described with dignity; enemy nations (Moab, Edom, Philistia) are reduced to household objects.

— PNEUMA
